subject: Request: comprehensive subprocessor & cloud operator dependency deep-dive
messages:
From: Michelle Lang <michelle.lang@procure.finbank.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: vendorsecurity@finbank.com
Date: 2027-04-25 09:12 -0700
Subject: Request: comprehensive subprocessor & cloud operator dependency deep-dive

Hi Naomi,

Hope you’re well. As part of FinBank Services’ annual third-party risk refresh, we need an up-to-date, machine-readable subprocessor roster and a cloud-operator dependency deep-dive for Redwood’s hosted and dedicated offerings. Specifically we are asking for:

- A current list of subprocessors (name, country, role, processing purpose, data types handled).
- An operator roster for any cloud or node operators (region, operator name/organization, contact owner) and whether operator access is single-tenant/dedicated or shared.
- A short summary of change-notice policies: how Redwood notifies customers about operator or region changes and the typical lead time for migrations or deprecations.
- Evidence: SOC 2 supplement or attestations related to operator controls, plus any recent penetration test summaries you can share.

We realize some contact-level info may be sensitive; a redacted roster is acceptable so long as it maps operators to region and role. Please provide the files in CSV/PDF and include any playbooks you have for operator failure/fallback behavior.

Requested by: 2027-04-28 COB (our audit window is tight). If you need to split materials across deliveries, please let us know what you can deliver by that date.

Thanks,
Michelle Lang
Senior Procurement Manager
FinBank Services
procurement@finbank.com

P.S. We also have one quick clarifying question: do you maintain per-tenant operator IP allowlists or only aggregate operator endpoint mappings?
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Lang <michelle.lang@procure.finbank.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-25 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: comprehensive subprocessor & cloud operator dependency deep-dive

Michelle — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. We can meet this request but will need to coordinate a couple of items internally: scope of redaction for contact-level data, and confirmation on whether you require per-tenant IP allowlists or if a region/operator mapping suffices.

Proposed delivery plan:
- 2027-04-27: redacted operator roster (CSV) + operator fallback playbook (PDF) + SOC2 supplementary evidence (PDF).
- If you need per-tenant IPs, we’ll need additional time for approval (legal & infra) — please confirm.

I’ve looped in our Security and Sales leads to own the technical mapping and the account confirmation. If that plan works, we’ll send the first bundle on Tuesday.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Working on the operator mapping. FYI: we have three operator profiles in scope for FinBank’s regions (us-west, us-east, eu-central): 
- Region operators managed by cloud partners (shared operator model)
- Dedicated node operators for Redwood Dedicated customers in the US (single-tenant operator engagements)
- Third-party edge operator (partner) used for EU fallthroughs

I’ll create operator_roster_redacted.csv with columns: region, operator_role, operator_org, operator_type (shared/dedicated), data_classes_handled, last_audit_date. For contact fields I’ll include "redacted" unless Kimberly advises otherwise.

I’ll also draft a short operator_fallback_playbook_v1.pdf describing automated routing, fallback to alternate region/operator, and customer notification timelines (typically 30 days for planned deprecation; 72 hours for operational failover with compensating controls).

— Karthik
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: comprehensive subprocessor & cloud operator dependency deep-dive

Michelle — attaching the requested materials. Per our earlier note, we have redacted contact-level information where it would reveal personnel PII or internal ops passwords; the mapping shows operator organization, region, operator_type, data classes, and last audit date.

Attachments (1 of 3 delivered):
- operator_roster_redacted.csv — region/operator mapping with redaction applied to personal contact fields.
- operator_fallback_playbook_v1.pdf — brief playbook that describes routing, automated fallbacks, expected notification timelines, and escalation steps.
- SOC2-Supplementary-evidence.pdf — relevant excerpts from our SOC2 report and a short supplement describing operator controls and shared-responsibility boundaries.

Short answers to your clarifying questions:
- Per-tenant IP allowlists: we do not publish per-tenant operator IPs as a standard artifact. We can provide per-customer allowlist guidance under a separate request and with appropriate approvals.
- Lead time for operator/region deprecation: planned deprecations are communicated with a minimum of 30 days and coordinated with customers; emergency operator failovers are executed as needed with post-event notifications.

Next steps: please confirm receipt and whether you need any additional detail (e.g., a non-redacted roster under an NDA, or per-tenant network artifacts). If you want an on-call walkthrough of the playbook with your security team, we can schedule a 45-minute session next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Attachments: operator_roster_redacted.csv (CSV), operator_fallback_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF), SOC2-Supplementary-evidence.pdf (PDF)
